title: Hot Blueberry and Cinnamon Infusion
excerpt: A comforting hot drink for cold afternoons, where the natural sweetness of blueberries blends with the spiced aroma of cinnamon.
imageAlt: Glass cup of hot blueberry and cinnamon infusion, steaming, with a cinnamon stick inside.
steps: In a small pot, pour the 2 1/2 cups of water and add the cinnamon stick together with the Fresh Pick blueberries.
Bring the mixture to medium-high heat until it comes to a boil.
Once it is boiling, reduce the heat to the minimum, cover the pot and let it simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Our high-mountain blueberries grown in Guasca will release all their juice and color; use a wooden spoon to gently mash a few of the berries against the side of the pot to intensify the flavor.
Remove from the heat, add the teaspoon of lemon juice, cover again and let the infusion rest for 3 minutes.

Strain the infusion as you serve it into your favorite cups, or, if you prefer, leave a few whole blueberries at the bottom to eat with a spoon. Add honey to taste if you want an extra touch of sweetness.
tips: You can save the blueberries left in the strainer to add to your breakfast oatmeal or mix with yogurt.
To keep the natural bloom and freshness of your Fresh Pick blueberries at home, keep the box in the refrigerator and wash them only right before making your recipe.
